findings.claim: women sit in a separate section - either an upper gallery (a mechitza) or a partitioned area to the side; the dfn defines mechitza as 'The women's gallery in an Orthodox synagogue'.
findings.truth: A mechitza is the screen or partition that divides the men's seating from the women's seating. A gallery is one seating arrangement, not the meaning of the word.
findings.evidence: Standard Jewish usage; the lesson's own knowledge check 4 already defines mechitza as a partition.

findings.claim: Reform communities have ordained women as rabbis since the early twentieth century in America and since the late twentieth century in the UK.
findings.truth: The first woman ordained as a rabbi in the United States was Sally Priesand, in 1972 (Hebrew Union College). Britain's first was Jackie Tabick, in 1975 (Leo Baeck College). Regina Jonas, ordained in Germany in 1935, was the first anywhere.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia: Sally Priesand; Wikipedia: Jackie Tabick.

findings.truth: The congregation was founded on 15 April 1840. Its first synagogue building, in Burton Street, opened on 27 January 1842.

findings.claim: the significance of the ner tamid recalling the Temple menorah (1 Kings 8) - repeated in the 6-mark mark scheme as '(1 Kings)'. Students are told to cite this as a source of authority.
findings.truth: 1 Kings 8 is Solomon's prayer at the dedication of the Temple and says nothing about the menorah. The command for a lamp to burn continually is Exodus 27:20-21, repeated at Leviticus 24:2-4.

findings.claim: This naming of the sub-tradition is exactly what the mark scheme rewards.
findings.truth: An invented claim about the board's mark scheme. House rule forbids quoting or characterising board mark schemes; the point can be made as a content point instead.
findings.evidence: CHECK_PROMPT_GENERIC.md copyright-distancing rule; no such wording exists in the specification.

findings.claim: The sixth practice question in every lesson is labelled '2 marks - State / Give' and asks for two items (L1 Hannah, L2 Yosef, L3 Isaac, L4 Naomi).
findings.truth: This paper sets two five-part questions per religion, worth 1, 1, 4, 6 and 12 marks. There is no 2-mark question. The short parts are worth 1 mark and ask for one item. Each has been retuned to a 1-mark question asking for one item.
findings.evidence: spec 4.4.1 and 'Specification at a glance' (assessment section, lines 244-275 and 1820-1840).

findings.claim: This contrast is exactly what gains marks.
findings.truth: Another invented claim about how answers are marked. Same rule as F5.

findings.claim: 'Name the two main collections that make up the Talmud.' labelled 1 mark, with the mark scheme saying 'both required for full credit'.
findings.truth: A 1-mark part asks for one item. Asking for two items for a single mark misrepresents the question form and the mark scheme.
findings.evidence: spec 4.4.1; the 1-mark parts of the five-part question.

findings.claim: Jewish teaching holds that 'the life is in the blood' (Leviticus 17:11) - quoted twice, once in the body and once in the Key Fact box.
findings.truth: Leviticus 17:11 reads 'For the life of the flesh is in the blood'. The quotation marks make the shortened form a misquotation.

findings.claim: The Board of Deputies of British Jews, which represents the whole Jewish community...
findings.truth: The Board is the main representative body but membership is voluntary and most Charedi synagogues are not affiliated, so it does not represent the whole community.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia: Board of Deputies of British Jews.

findings.claim: trefah - 'Hebrew word meaning forbidden or unfit'.
findings.truth: Trefah literally means 'torn', from the animal torn by wild beasts in Exodus 22:30; 'forbidden' is the working sense. The gloss given is the standard GCSE one and costs no marks.

findings.claim: A waiting period (typically six hours in Ashkenazi communities) must pass between eating meat and dairy.
findings.truth: Six hours is the majority custom but it is not specifically Ashkenazi: it is the Sephardi rule, while Jews of German descent commonly wait three hours and the Dutch custom is one hour. 'Typically six hours, depending on community custom' would be safer. Not examinable detail.
findings.evidence: Standard kashrut practice; not set by the specification.

findings.claim: Bat Mitzvah is given as age 12 for girls throughout the lesson.
findings.truth: Twelve is the Orthodox age. In most Reform and Liberal communities girls become Bat Mitzvah at 13, the same age as boys. The body text hedges ('in many communities, 12 for girls') and the age is not set by the specification, so no mark is at risk; worth adding on the next content pass.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia: Bar and bat mitzvah; spec 3.1.6.2 lists 'Bar and Bat Mitzvah' with no age.

findings.claim: Lesson descriptions run to 117 (L2), 112 (L3) and 118 (L4) characters.
findings.truth: The house limit is under 100 characters. Not a fact error, but the validator will flag these three rows if it is run over the whole unit.

findings.claim: The '2 marks - State / Give' sixth question is not local to this unit: the label appears in all 20 religious-studies-aqa units fetched for the programme (10 to 36 hits each).
findings.truth: Options: (a) sweep the whole religious-studies-aqa subject with one script, converting every '2 marks' label to a 1-mark one-item question, as done by hand here; (b) leave the other units to their own retro checks, which will each repeat this work; (c) accept the 2-mark form as house scaffolding and stop flagging it. Recommendation: (a) - it is a mechanical relabel, the form does not exist on this paper, and the other 19 units carry the same defect whether or not their content is checked.
findings.ruling: Noted: the 2-mark label is being fixed unit by unit as each RS unit passes through the loop.

summary: Content, scripture and answer keys are sound: all 20 knowledge-check keys and all four match sets are correct, and the festival dates, mourning periods, kashrut rules and Hebrew terms check out. The errors are an exam-form one repeated in every lesson (a 2-mark question the paper does not set), two invented mark-scheme claims, a wrong scripture reference for the ner tamid, a truncated Leviticus 17:11, and three factual slips (mechitza, women's ordination dates, the Board of Deputies).
